title: Two minutes late
setting: Saturday, late afternoon. It's Kenji's birthday, and Okaasan has gone out to buy his cake at the family's usual cake shop, which only takes cash. Yuki doesn't pick up, so Okaasan leaves her three voicemails: one from the queue at the bank by the station, one once she has her cash, and one outside the cake shop.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: yuki? okaasan da kedo. ima ne, eki no mae no ginkou ni, okane oroshi ni kiteru no.
lines.ja: ユキ？お母さんだけど。今ね、駅の前の銀行に、お金下ろしに来てるの。
lines.kana: ゆき？おかあさんだけど。いまね、えきのまえのぎんこうに、おかねおろしにきてるの。
lines.english: Yuki? It's Mum. I'm at the bank by the station, getting some cash out.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kenji no tanjoubi no keeki, itsumo no mise de kau n da kedo, asoko, kaado tsukaenai no yo.
lines.ja: ケンジの誕生日のケーキ、いつもの店で買うんだけど、あそこ、カード使えないのよ。
lines.kana: けんじのたんじょうびのけーき、いつものみせでかうんだけど、あそこ、かーどつかえないのよ。
lines.english: I'm getting Kenji's birthday cake at the usual place, but they don't take cards.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: demo, doyoubi da kara ka, hito ga ookute ne. mou nijuppun mo junban matteru no.
lines.ja: でも、土曜日だからか、人が多くてね。もう二十分も順番待ってるの。
lines.kana: でも、どようびだからか、ひとがおおくてね。もうにじゅっぷんもじゅんばんまってるの。
lines.english: But it's packed, maybe because it's Saturday. I've already been waiting my turn for twenty minutes.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: maa, mise wa rokuji made aiteru kara, shimaru mae ni wa ikeru to omou kedo.
lines.ja: まあ、店は六時まで開いてるから、閉まる前には行けると思うけど。
lines.kana: まあ、みせはろくじまであいてるから、しまるまえにはいけるとおもうけど。
lines.english: Well, the shop's open till six, so I should get there before it closes.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: yuki, mata okaasan. yatto okane oroseta wa. kekkyoku sanjuppun yo.
lines.ja: ユキ、またお母さん。やっとお金下ろせたわ。結局三十分よ。
lines.kana: ゆき、またおかあさん。やっとおかねおろせたわ。けっきょくさんじゅっぷんよ。
lines.english: Yuki, Mum again. I finally got the cash out. Thirty minutes, in the end!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: mae no chiisai kodomo ga ne, zutto mada? mada? tte ittete.
lines.ja: 前の小さい子どもがね、ずっと「まだ？まだ？」って言ってて。
lines.kana: まえのちいさいこどもがね、ずっと「まだ？まだ？」っていってて。
lines.english: The little kid in front of me kept going, 'Is it our turn yet? Is it our turn yet?'

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: chanto junban matte ne tte iwareteta wa. kenji mo mukashi wa sou datta wa ne.
lines.ja: 「ちゃんと順番待ってね」って言われてたわ。ケンジも昔はそうだったわね。
lines.kana: 「ちゃんとじゅんばんまってね」っていわれてたわ。けんじもむかしはそうだったわね。
lines.english: He kept getting told, 'Wait your turn nicely, OK?' Kenji was just like that when he was little.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: a, mou rokuji juppun mae! hayaku ikanai to, mise shimatchau. jaa ne.
lines.ja: あ、もう六時十分前！早く行かないと、店閉まっちゃう。じゃあね。
lines.kana: あ、もうろくじじゅっぷんまえ！はやくいかないと、みせしまっちゃう。じゃあね。
lines.english: Oh, it's already ten to six! If I don't hurry, the shop'll close. Bye!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: yuki, nando mo gomen ne. mise, mou shimatteta no.
lines.ja: ユキ、何度もごめんね。店、もう閉まってたの。
lines.kana: ゆき、なんどもごめんね。みせ、もうしまってたの。
lines.english: Yuki, sorry for all the calls. The shop was already closed.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: nifun osokatta no yo. sekkaku okane oroshita noni.
lines.ja: 二分遅かったのよ。せっかくお金下ろしたのに。
lines.kana: にふんおそかったのよ。せっかくおかねおろしたのに。
lines.english: I was two minutes too late. And after all that trouble getting the cash out, too.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sore de onegai na n da kedo, kaeri ni keeki katte kite kurenai? jikan aitetara de ii kara.
lines.ja: それでお願いなんだけど、帰りにケーキ買ってきてくれない？時間空いてたらでいいから。
lines.kana: それでおねがいなんだけど、かえりにけーきかってきてくれない？じかんあいてたらでいいから。
lines.english: So, a favour: could you pick up a cake on your way home? Only if you've got time.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: eki no naka no mise nara, hachiji made aiteru kara. okane wa ato de ageru ne.
lines.ja: 駅の中の店なら、八時まで開いてるから。お金はあとであげるね。
lines.kana: えきのなかのみせなら、はちじまであいてるから。おかねはあとであげるね。
lines.english: The shop inside the station is open till eight. I'll give you the money later.

choices.english: The bank queue was so long that she gave up on getting cash, so she wants Yuki to pay for the cake by card.
She got her cash, but the cake shop had closed by the time she got there, so she's asking Yuki to pick up a cake on the way home.
She bought the cake in time, but now she's out of cash, so she's asking Yuki to stop at the bank on the way home.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-3: Okaasan is at the bank getting cash for Kenji's birthday cake, because the usual shop doesn't take cards, and she has been waiting her turn for twenty minutes. Line 5: she finally gets the cash, and in line 8 she hurries off before the shop closes. Lines 9-10: it was already closed, and she was two minutes late. Lines 11-12: she asks Yuki to buy a cake on her way home at the shop inside the station, which is open till eight. A is wrong because she did get the cash (line 5), and the cake shop doesn't take cards anyway (line 2). C is wrong because she never got the cake (line 9). She has the cash, and the favour is buying the cake.

questions.english: You're out for dinner with Kenta. When it's time to pay, he says: "Apparently this place doesn't take cards." You have no cash on you, and there's a konbini right by. Tell him you'll go and get some cash.
questions.ja: この店、カード使えないって。
questions.kana: このみせ、かーどつかえないって。
questions.answer: Say you'll go and get cash with okane o orosu plus -te kuru (go, do it, come back): chotto okane oroshite kuru ne. Not okane o toru.

modelAnswers.romaji: e, honto? jaa, chotto okane oroshite kuru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: え、ほんと？じゃあ、ちょっとお金下ろしてくるね。
modelAnswers.english: Really? Then I'll just go and grab some cash.

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, konbini de okane oroshite kuru kara, chotto mattete.
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、コンビニでお金下ろしてくるから、ちょっと待ってて。
modelAnswers.english: Then I'll go get some cash at the konbini. Wait here a sec.

questions.explanation: Getting cash from a machine is orosu ('bring down'). Okaasan went to the bank okane oroshi ni (line 1), finally okane oroseta (line 5), and complains sekkaku okane oroshita noni (line 10). Adding -te kuru makes it 'go and do it, then come back', which is what you say as you head off. okane o toru, the word-for-word 'take money', sounds like taking someone's money. Casual okane dasu also works. Kenta's cue is the same problem Okaasan has in line 2 (kaado tsukaenai).

questions.english: In her last message, Okaasan says the shop inside the station is "hachiji made aiteru". What does she mean?
questions.ja: お母さんは、駅の中の店について何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: おかあさんは、えきのなかのみせについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa, eki no naka no mise ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: It opens at eight, so Yuki would have to wait around.
Yuki is free until eight, so she has time to go.
It's open until eight, so Yuki can still get there in time.

questions.explanation: Line 12: eki no naka no mise nara, hachiji made aiteru kara. A shop that aiteru is open, and made says until when, so it's open till eight. Okaasan said the same about the cake shop in line 4 (rokuji made aiteru). A would be hachiji ni aku, because plain aku is the moment a shop opens. B mixes it up with the other aiteru, one line earlier: jikan aitetara de ii kara (line 11) means 'only if you're free'. That one is about Yuki's time, not the shop.

questions.english: It's ten at night. Kenta says he's heading out to the shop by the station and asks if you want anything. You know that shop closes at nine. Tell him it's already closed.
questions.ja: 今から駅の前の店に買い物に行くけど、何か欲しいものある？
questions.kana: いまからえきのまえのみせにかいものにいくけど、なにかほしいものある？
questions.romaji: ima kara eki no mae no mise ni kaimono ni iku kedo, nanika hoshii mono aru?
questions.answer: Tell him it's shut with shimatteru (is closed): ano mise, mou shimatteru yo. For the closing time, use plain shimaru: kuji ni shimaru.

modelAnswers.romaji: e, ano mise, mou shimatteru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: え、あの店、もう閉まってるよ。

modelAnswers.romaji: ano mise, kuji ni shimaru kara, mou shimatteru n ja nai?
modelAnswers.ja: あの店、九時に閉まるから、もう閉まってるんじゃない？
modelAnswers.english: That shop closes at nine, so it's probably shut by now, isn't it?

questions.explanation: A shop closing is shimaru. Okaasan says shimaru mae ni (before it closes, line 4), mise shimatchau (the shop'll close, line 8) and mise, mou shimatteta (it was already closed, line 9). For how the shop is right now, use shimatteru. shimeru is what the staff do when they close up, so it fits when you ask them (nanji ni shimemasu ka?). Casual owaru also works: mou owatteru yo.

questions.english: The little kid in front of Okaasan kept asking "mada?". What was he told?
questions.ja: 前の子どもは、何と言われていましたか？
questions.kana: まえのこどもは、なんといわれていましたか？
questions.romaji: mae no kodomo wa, nan to iwarete imashita ka?

choices.english: Wait for your (anata no) turn nicely, OK?
choices.romaji: chanto anata no ban o matte ne.

choices.english: Don't get the order mixed up, OK?

questions.explanation: Line 7: chanto junban matte ne. Waiting your turn is junban o matsu, and in casual speech the o drops. Okaasan uses it about herself in line 3 (mou nijuppun mo junban matteru). Standing in the queue itself would be narabu. B is English 'wait for your turn' word for word: Japanese leaves out 'your' here, and anata sounds cold from a parent to a small child. C sounds close (junban, machi-) but means 'don't get the order wrong'. The kid was impatient, not muddled.
